title: Phase-Synchronized TECS Integrating TI-tACS and rTMS: Modeling, Hardware Implementation, and In Vivo Neurophysiological Validation.
authors: Wang, Tingyu; Guo, Miaomiao; Cui, Chao; Wei, Yujia; Zhao, Xiuzhi; Zheng, Weiran; Wang, Alan; Xu, Guizhi
journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
one_liner_zh: 该文研究经颅电磁联合刺激的神经调控硬件与动物验证，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Conventional noninvasive neuromodulation is constrained by trade-offs among field strength, focality, and penetration. We propose a phase-synchronized transcranial electromagnetic combined stimulation (TECS) approach that concurrently combines temporal interference transcranial alternating current stimulation (TI-tACS) with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) to improve the local intensity-focality trade-off in the motor cortex. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate a phase-synchronized concurrent TI-tACS + rTMS paradigm. METHODS: Finite-element simulations quantified the peak magnitude-based stimulation metric in the target M1 region, together with the equivalent focal area and effective penetration depth under a half-maximum criterion. A phase-synchronized TECS system was implemented and evaluated in rats using rotarod performance, c-Fos immunofluorescence, and histology, with comparisons to TI-tACS alone, rTMS alone, and a shamlike control condition. RESULTS: TECS produced the highest peak target-region electric-field value (178.0 V/m) while maintaining a much smaller focal area than rTMS alone (8.3 vs. 76.0 mm2) and greater penetration than TI-tACS alone (2.1 vs. 1.2 mm). In vivo, TECS produced the longest rotarod latency on Day $7(288.5 \pm 16.4 ~\text s; \text n=6$ rats/group; daily values averaged over three trials/rat), exceeding the control, TItACS, and rTMS groups by 75.3%, 15.3%, and 19.4%, respectively. TECS also induced the highest c-Fos activation, with corresponding increases of 50.1%, 9.4%, and 12.8%, respectively. Histology revealed no overt abnormalities across conditions. CONCLUSION: Phase-synchronized TECS enhances focal electric-field intensity and neuronal activation, translating to improved motor performance. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed TECS platform provides a promising neuroengineering approach for targeted noninvasive brain stimulation, supported by simulationdefined field metrics and in vivo feasibility and safety validation.
abstract_zh: 目的：传统非侵入性神经调控受限于场强、聚焦性和穿透深度之间的权衡。我们提出一种相位同步经颅电磁联合刺激（TECS）方法，将时间干扰经颅交流电刺激（TI-tACS）与重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）同步结合，以改善运动皮层中局部强度-聚焦性权衡。据我们所知，这是首个研究相位同步并发TI-tACS + rTMS范式的研究。方法：有限元模拟量化了目标M1区域中基于峰值幅度的刺激指标，以及半最大值准则下的等效聚焦面积和有效穿透深度。我们实现了一种相位同步TECS系统，并在大鼠中通过旋转杆性能、c-Fos免疫荧光和组织学进行评估，与单独TI-tACS、单独rTMS及假刺激对照条件进行比较。结果：TECS产生了最高的目标区域峰值电场值（178.0 V/m），同时保持比单独rTMS更小的聚焦面积（8.3 vs. 76.0 mm²），且穿透深度大于单独TI-tACS（2.1 vs. 1.2 mm）。在体内实验中，TECS在第7天产生了最长的旋转杆潜伏期（288.5 ± 16.4 秒；每组n=6只大鼠；每日值取每只大鼠三次试验的平均值），分别超过对照组、TI-tACS组和rTMS组75.3%、15.3%和19.4%。TECS还诱导了最高的c-Fos激活，相应增加分别为50.1%、9.4%和12.8%。组织学显示各条件下无明显异常。结论：相位同步TECS增强了聚焦电场强度和神经元激活，转化为改善的运动表现。意义：所提出的TECS平台为靶向非侵入性脑刺激提供了一种有前景的神经工程方法，并得到模拟定义的场指标及体内可行性和安全性验证的支持。
